subject: Paygo -> Commit conversion pathway and cushion mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@hightide.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@hightide.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Query: moving from Paygo to a commit + cushion model

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We like Redwood's latency and the KV cache savings you showed. We've been running pay-as-you-go with you for the last 3 months and want to get pricing into our annual plan.

High-level ask: our finance team wants a 3-year committed pricing path but also needs a way to handle spikes without being penalized by very high overage rates. Specifically: can you outline a mechanism that lets us convert paygo spend into a committed floor, and a separate short-term "cushion" or burst band at a predictable on-demand overage rate?

Details:
- Current average monthly tokens (gen + embeddings): ~12B tokens/month (see attached forecast).
- We expect occasional spikes up to 2x for product launches (1-2 weeks).
- Key constraints: fixed budget cadence (quarterly) and a one-sheet for procurement explaining minimum spend, overage math, and true-up cadence.

Can you share (1) proposed commit tiers and discounts vs paygo, (2) suggested overage rates for cushion/burst, (3) true-up cadence (monthly/quarterly), and (4) any flexibility to convert remaining paygo credits into committed spend on contract signing?

Appreciate a short proposal we can take to procurement — thanks.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform
Hightide AI

Attachments: usage-forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, procurement@hightide.ai

Subject: Re: Query: moving from Paygo to a commit + cushion model

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and the forecast — helpful. High level reply below; I'll follow with a short formal proposal PDF if you want to share with procurement.

1) Commit tiers and discounting- We typically price commits in bands tied to baseline tokens/month. For your volume (12B/mo) we'd propose an initial 12–18B/mo tier with a 20% discount vs current Hosted paygo list rates. Larger committed bands (>=24B/mo) get stepped discounts up to 30% depending on term length (36 months gets max).

2) Cushion / burst mechanics- Two-layer approach we recommend: a) Soft cushion (buffer band) equivalent to 20% of committed monthly tokens that carries an on-demand overage rate at ~1.4x paygo list; b) Hard burst above cushion billed at paygo list but eligible for monthly true-up credits if average monthly usage stays within 10% of committed for the quarter. This keeps short spikes cheap while disincentivizing sustained over-usage.

3) True-up cadence- Quarterly true-up by default; monthly true-up is available for a modest admin fee. True-ups convert overage spend beyond cushion into committed credit at the committed effective unit price if the quarter's average justifies it.

4) Conversion of paygo credits- We can allow existing paygo credits to be applied toward the first-month committed invoice if contract signed within 60 days of proposal date.

I attached a one-page summary and a sample term sheet. If this direction looks reasonable, we can do a redline-safe term sheet and get legal engaged.

Next steps: is procurement looking for a single-line item (one committed band) or a staircase (e.g., 12/18/24B breakpoints) we should model?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Hightide-MA-3yr-draft.pdf (term sheet)

Subject: Fwd: Query: moving from Paygo to a commit + cushion model

Lauren / Karthik —

Looping you in to confirm concessions and pricing guardrails before I send the formal proposal to Hightide. Thread below for context.

My proposed structure for approval:
- Term: 36 months; initial commit = 12B tokens/month; optional step-up to 18B at 12-month mark (client-controlled).
- Effective discount: 20% off paygo list at 12B; 25% at 18B; 30% at >=24B (all subject to term).
- Soft cushion: 20% of committed tokens billed at 1.4x paygo list.
- Hard burst: billed at list; if quarterly average <= committed + 10% we convert up to 50% of hard burst spend for that quarter into committed credit at the committed price (one-time true-up credit).
- Paygo credit conversion: allow credits <= one month's historical spend to be applied to the first invoice if signed in 60 days.

I recommend approving the cushion band and the 1.4x overage rate for short bursts — it gives Hightide predictable math and keeps MRR reasonable. Any objections or guardrails you'd like before I send?

—Ben

Ben —

This looks fine to send with two small exceptions to protect us:

1) Cushion cap window: make the 20% cushion only available for bursts up to 21 days per quarter; anything beyond that moves into hard burst immediately. This prevents customers from treating the cushion as an ongoing top-up.
2) True-up conversion limit: limit quarterly conversion of hard burst spend to 50% of the quarter's committed bill (so we don't convert sustained overage into free committed volume).

Otherwise approve. Add a short example table in the one-pager showing math for a 2x spike week (we should show before/after billing). After you add the two clarifications above, send to Alex with the attached term sheet and I'll join procurement call if they request it.

—Lauren
